approved: Defence (Honour General Sir John Monash) Amendment Bill 2018
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would give General Sir John Monash the rank of Australian Field Marshal after his death.
It would do this through a promotion that applies only to him, with clauses limiting any resulting claims, precedence, or entitlements.
The bill would have no financial impact, and the explanatory memorandum does not specify a start date.
The bill would posthumously promote General Sir John Monash to Australian Field Marshal.
The bill would restrict the promotion's effects to this specific case.
The bill would limit claims, precedence, or entitlements arising from the promotion.
General Sir John Monash and his estate are affected.

The speaker seconded the Defence (Honour General Sir John Monash) Amendment Bill 2018, arguing that Sir John Monash should be posthumously elevated to field marshal to recognise his outstanding World War I achievements, supported by Tim Fischer's campaign and Professor Roland Perry's book. The bill includes safeguard clauses to avoid unintended consequences.
